title: Dynamic response budgets — playbook & lab notes
content:
Context: quick brain-dump for a small scoped feature we can prototype in hosted API: dynamic response budgets. Goal is to let product teams define per-route/per-customer budgets (token budget, latency budget, confidence floor) that the runtime enforces via lightweight heuristics and model-polymorphism. This is intentionally a lab/playbook doc — rough ideas, user stories, tests, and rollout checklist.

Why: many customers want predictable unit cost while preserving apparent quality. Current levers (quantization, batching, model selection) are too coarse and disconnected from the app's intent. A small control plane that maps app-level SLOs to runtime knobs would make it easier to hit cost and latency targets without constant manual tuning.

Core concept (1-paragraph):
- A response budget = a compact, typed policy attached to a route or session. Fields: token_budget_hint (soft), latency_slo_ms (soft/hard), min_confidence_score (optional), fallback_policy (model_fallback | truncate | rerank), economy_profile (conservative | balanced | quality-first). The platform translates the policy into per-call decisions: choose model variant, target max_output_tokens, enable prefix/kvcaching, and decide whether to run a light reranker.

User stories (raw):
- As an internal PM building a chat feature, I want to set a 300-token soft budget and balanced economy on /chat so the monthly bill stays predictable for free-tier users.
- As a platform engineer, I want the runtime to automatically pick cheaper model variants when token_budget_hint is low and fall back to higher-capacity models if the initial output fails the min_confidence_score.
- As an SRE, I want per-route telemetry for budget hits/misses (how often target tokens < actual) and automated alerts when fallback policies are used >5% of requests.
- As an experimenter, I want a canary mode where the budget is enforced only for a percentage of traffic and the platform records quality delta.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API: route config accepts a small JSON policy (token_budget_hint, latency_slo_ms, economy_profile, fallback_policy).
- Runtime: When policy present, runtime can change model variant and output token cap per-request.
- Telemetry: metrics emitted: budget_applied, budget_exceeded, fallback_invoked, avg_latency, token_consumption.
- UX: Console shows per-route budget usage heatmap and example traces for budget-triggered fallbacks.

Edge cases and heuristics:
- Soft vs hard: token_budget_hint is advisory; runtime should try to keep within but allow overshoot for high-confidence outputs. There should be an explicit hard_token_limit flag for strict enforcement (truncate output).
- Conversational state: budgets should be evaluated against delta tokens per-turn rather than total session length to reduce surprise truncation.
- Multi-model fallbacks: prefer same-architecture cheaper variant first (quantized) before switching families to avoid big distribution shifts.

Experiment matrix (lab plan):
1) Small-scope A/B: route-level budget (300 vs 800 tokens) on a low-traffic assistant flow (internally simulated). Measure: BLEU/ROUGE-ish quality proxy, user satisfaction proxy (thumbs), token cost delta, latency.
2) Confidence-aware fallback: generate with cheap model + cheap reranker vs single expensive model. Measure output quality and cost.
3) Latency SLO test: enforce latency_slo_ms=200ms soft and instrument tail-latency percentiles.

Instrumentations to add (quick):
- New tags on traces: budget_requested, budget_enforced, enforced_model_variant, reason_for_fallback.
- New counters: budget_attempts, budget_hits, budget_misses; histograms: token_usage_per_response.

Rough API sketch (example request):
POST /v1/generate
Headers: x-route-config: {"token_budget_hint":300, "latency_slo_ms":250, "economy_profile":"balanced", "fallback_policy":"model_fallback"}
Body: standard prompt + session_id
Behavior: runtime reads header, picks variant, sets max_tokens goal, attaches trace.

Quick UX copy for Console (ideas):
- "Response budgets" panel with toggle, sample traces, and a simulated "what-if" slider to preview cost impact.
- Per-customer defaults + overrides per-route.

Rollout plan (canary → gradual):
- Stage 0: internal sandbox only — add flags, metrics, and a debug mode that returns 'budget_decision' in headers.
- Stage 1: opt-in beta for 5 customers and internal QA. Collect signal for quality regressions.
- Stage 2: public toggle in Console, default off; telemetry baseline and user docs.

Risks / unknowns:
- Quality regressions invisible to simple proxies: need small, labeled eval sets per-route to catch semantic failures.
- Customers may misuse soft budgets expecting hard limits — must surface clear UX and warnings.
- Complex session flows (multi-turn clarifications) may accumulate tokens unpredictably; need tooling to surface per-turn deltas.

Open questions: (short)
- What should default economy_profile map to in practice? (quantize+smaller-context vs smaller model family)
- How to support embeddings/other ops where token budgets don't directly translate?
- Legal: are there regulatory considerations for silently changing model families because of cost? (flag for enterprise customers)

Low-effort prototype steps (next 2 weeks):
- Add header-based route-config parsing to gateway and stub a budget_decision header back for debug. (Eng: Diego)
- Add a small simulated workload harness to run A/B tests across model variants (Eng: Ruth).
- Build minimal Console widget showing per-route budget hits (Prod: Sanjay + Evelyn).

Notes to self:
- Keep this MVP narrow: focus on text-generation routes initially. Save reranking and embeddings for v2.
- Reuse existing rollout infra (canary percent, autopause).
- Pair with a tiny eval suite per-route (5–10 prompts) to detect catastrophic failures quickly.

TODO checklist:
- [ ] Wire header parsing and budget_decision debug header
- [ ] Add metrics and tags to tracing
- [ ] Implement model selection hook (cheap variant fallback) in runtime shim
- [ ] Create internal demo workspace + sample route configs
- [ ] Draft Console copy and create mock screenshots
- [ ] Write short beta onboarding doc for customers

Loose brainstorm bullets (discardable):
- Allow users to attach a "business rule" to budget: e.g., "always prefer accuracy for messages flagged as payments"
- Auto-suggest budgets from historical token usage + desired billing cap
- Offer an "elastic buffer" token pool shared across sessions for a customer to allow occasional overage

If this lands well, v2 could include: per-user budgets, ML-driven budget tuning, and automatic mini-evals that flip fallback policies when regressions detected.

End of scratchpad — keep it messy; will turn into a short PRD after 1–2 experiments.

References/links in my head while writing: quick threads about session-presets, model-fallback design doc, and recent cost SLO discussions. Will paste links above as I gather them.
